root_cause: The English selector could become active while the page remained Dutch because the translation pipeline treated any single provider/batch failure or non-bare JSON response as fatal. setLocale then reverted the locale, and the v1 browser cache could preserve stale Dutch fallbacks for the English key.
prevention: Translation parsing must accept valid JSON arrays even when the provider wraps them in a JSON code fence or surrounding text.
A failed translation batch must not roll back successful batches or revert the selected locale.
The English translation cache version must be bumped after a broken translation contract so stale fallbacks cannot survive the repair.
Large pages must use bounded translation batches with independent failure isolation.
evidence: user production report 2026-09-21: clicking English changed no website text
